title: Coinbase's CTO shares the traits that all standout engineers have
excerpt: Coinbase CTO Rob Witoff said engineers will increasingly have to make much more challenging strategic decisions.
content_html:
The traits that make engineers stand out, according to Coinbase’s CTO

By Ana Altchek

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

AI can do a lot, but it can't replace human taste and judgment.

Coinbase CTO Rob Witoff told Business Insider that those are the traits that make engineering candidates stand out nowadays. As AI takes over routine tasks, Witoff said engineers will increasingly be expected to tackle "much harder strategy decisions."

That means the company wants developers who aren't "working in a single lane," he said.

"We want people that can step back and really understand why they're doing something," Witoff said.

What it means to have 'taste and judgment'

In a July blog post on the topic, Coinbase describes taste and judgement as "Knowing what's actually worth building, telling a genuinely good solution from one that only looks right, and sensing when to override the model."

Witoff said strong taste doesn't necessarily come from years of industry experience. For many candidates, it can come from using the company's products or participating in the crypto market.

"You can develop that judgment a lot of ways, but having that as a capability inside is what's really important," Witoff said.

Rather than grading how quickly an engineer can write raw syntax or complete algorithmic puzzles, Witoff said that judgement comes into play when workers have to determine which trade-offs to make and when to reject what an AI model produces.

The company has rebuilt its engineering interview loop to keep pace with the change by testing how candidates direct AI, evaluate its output, and apply judgment where models fall short.

What matters less, Witoff said, is expertise with any single AI tool. With AI models evolving so rapidly, he said he avoids over-indexing on a single tool and instead prefers software engineers who are comfortable using a range of models.

The CTO's comments come after Coinbase laid off 14% of its workforce in May, or about 700 employees, saying AI is reshaping how the company operates.

At the time of the job cuts, CEO Brian Armstrong said the company would have "no pure managers" as it pivots to tiny teams, some of which will operate with engineers, designers, and product managers in a single role.

Armstrong also said in the layoff memo that AI was helping engineers "ship in days what used to take a team weeks."

According to Coinbase's most recent regulatory filing disclosing headcount, the company employed 4,951 employees as of December 2025, before the layoffs.

Why judgement and taste are becoming more important

Witoff isn't alone in arguing that judgment and taste are becoming the most valuable skills in technical hiring. Tech leaders, including Y Combinator cofounder Paul Graham and OpenAI President Greg Brockman, have said strong judgment is increasingly essential.

Witoff said engineers make up roughly half of the company's workforce, with more senior and principal engineers on staff than ever before. The company said it doesn't disclose specific employment numbers.

Coinbase is increasingly bringing those engineers into higher-level conversations, Witoff said, and AI tools are enabling many of them to solve problems in days that once took months or even quarters.

Now that one strong engineer can now do the work of a full team, and everyone has a fleet of agents working for them, engineers need to know how to direct teams and collaborate with agents and people across disciplines, Witoff said.

Witoff said humans still have an edge over AI in understanding other humans, making it increasingly important to focus on customer needs, which products to build, and when to build them. Today, even the strongest teams may spend just 20% to 30% of their time on those strategic questions, he said. Over time, he expects that share to climb to 95% as AI handles more repetitive work.

content_html_zh:
Coinbase 首席技术官表示，工程师脱颖而出的特质

作者：Ana Altchek 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

人工智能可以做很多事情，但它无法取代人类的品味和判断。

Coinbase 首席技术官 Rob Witoff 告诉《商业内幕》，这些正是当今工程候选人脱颖而出的特质。 威托夫表示，随着人工智能接管日常任务，工程师将越来越需要解决“更困难的战略决策”。

他说，这意味着该公司想要的开发商不是“在单一车道上工作”。

“我们希望人们能够退后一步，真正理解他们为什么要做某事，”维托夫说。

拥有“品味和判断力”意味着什么

在 7 月份一篇关于该主题的博客文章中，Coinbase 将品味和判断描述为“知道什么是真正值得构建的，区分真正好的解决方案和看起来正确的解决方案，并感知何时覆盖模型。”

维托夫表示，强烈的品味并不一定来自多年的行业经验。 对于许多候选人来说，它可以来自使用公司的产品或参与加密市场。

维托夫说：“你可以通过多种方式培养这种判断力，但将其作为一种内在能力才是真正重要的。”

Witoff 表示，不是对工程师编写原始语法或完成算法难题的速度进行评分，而是当工人必须确定要做出哪些权衡以及何时拒绝人工智能模型产生的结果时，判断力就会发挥作用。

该公司已经重建了工程面试循环，通过测试候选人如何指导人工智能、评估其输出以及在模型不足之处进行判断来跟上变化的步伐。

维托夫说，不那么重要的是任何单一人工智能工具的专业知识。 他表示，随着人工智能模型的发展如此之快，他避免对单一工具进行过度索引，而是更喜欢能够轻松使用一系列模型的软件工程师。

CTO 发表此番言论之前，Coinbase 在 5 月份解雇了 14% 的员工，即约 700 名员工，称人工智能正在重塑公司的运营方式。

在裁员时，首席执行官布莱恩·阿姆斯特朗表示，公司将“没有纯粹的经理”，因为公司将转向小型团队，其中一些团队将由工程师、设计师和产品经理担任单一角色。

阿姆斯特朗还在裁员备忘录中表示，人工智能正在帮助工程师“在几天内完成团队过去需要几周的时间”。

根据 Coinbase 最近披露的监管文件显示，截至 2025 年 12 月（裁员前），该公司雇用了 4,951 名员工。

为什么判断力和品味变得越来越重要

维托夫并不是唯一一个认为判断力和品味正在成为技术招聘中最有价值技能的人。 Y Combinator 联合创始人 Paul Graham 和 OpenAI 总裁 Greg Brockman 等科技领袖表示，强有力的判断力越来越重要。

维托夫表示，工程师约占公司员工的一半，高级工程师和首席工程师的数量比以往任何时候都多。 该公司表示没有透露具体的就业人数。

Witoff 表示，Coinbase 越来越多地让这些工程师参与更高级别的对话，人工智能工具使他们中的许多人能够在几天内解决曾经需要几个月甚至几个季度的问题。

Witoff 说，既然一名强大的工程师现在可以完成整个团队的工作，并且每个人都有一组为他们工作的代理，工程师需要知道如何指导团队并与跨学科的代理和人员协作。

维托夫表示，在理解其他人类方面，人类仍然比人工智能有优势，因此关注客户需求、构建哪些产品以及何时构建变得越来越重要。 他说，如今，即使是最强大的团队也可能只花费 20% 到 30% 的时间来解决这些战略问题。 随着时间的推移，他预计随着人工智能处理更多重复性工作，这一比例将攀升至 95%。
